contested.Length: 162.3 km (Neftegaz), 163 km (Gazprom design institute), 169 km (RIA Novosti), 174 km (Eurasia Expert)

validity.researcher_notes: The pipeline is confirmed as built and in service. Reported lengths differ by source: 162.3 km, 163 km, 169 km and 174 km. The longer figures may count the built route and the shorter ones the design route. Ownership caveat: Gazprom Yuzhnaya Osetiya operates only the 71 km South Ossetian section, so the whole line may not be held by Gazprom PJSC alone.

verifications.note: Gazprom deputy CEO said the pipeline cost 15 billion rubles ($476 million)

fills.researcher_notes: RIA Novosti, 26 August 2009, reports Gazprom's deputy chief executive saying the new pipeline cost 15 billion rubles, or 476 million US dollars. The sheet value is the dollar figure. Eurasia Expert also gives 15 billion rubles. The dollar amount is as reported in 2009.

The Operator cell is blank. A November 2020 page from Gazprom Transgaz Stavropol says its Mozdok line production unit maintains this pipeline, and Neftegaz (December 2018) says a joint company runs the South Ossetian section only. Neither states one operator for the whole line, so no value was staged. Not searched this pass.

fills.researcher_notes: Two pages state 252.5 million cubic metres per year, which is 0.2525 bcm per year and matches the recorded 0.25. A Gazprom design institute page and Neftegaz trade press, read in full.

verifications.note: states length 162.3 km (92 km in North Ossetia, 71 km in South Ossetia)
design length 162.3 km, actual length 174 km

fills.researcher_notes: Neftegaz states 162.3 km exactly, with the split of 92 km in North Ossetia and 71 km in South Ossetia. Eurasia Expert gives 162.3 km as the design length and says the built length is 174 km. The Gazprom design institute page rounds to 163 km, and RIA Novosti in 2009 said 169 km. The sheet value matches the most precise figures; the spread is noted in the validity record.

fills.researcher_notes: Three pages place the launch on 26 August 2009. Start year 2009 and start month 8.

verifications.note: December 2018: Russian gas flows to South Ossetia through the line; the line is loaded to under 15 percent

fills.researcher_notes: Neftegaz, 20 December 2018, says Russian gas is delivered to South Ossetia through the pipeline and that its load is under 15 percent. This is the newest explicit report of operation among the wiki citations. A Gazprom Transgaz Stavropol page from November 2020 is also cited but did not load in this pass.

verifications.note: Gazprom holds 100 percent of Gazprom Yuzhnaya Osetiya, which operates the South Ossetian section

fills.researcher_notes: Neftegaz, December 2018, says Gazprom is raising its share in Gazprom Yuzhnaya Osetiya to 100 percent, and that this company was created to operate the South Ossetian section (71 km) of the line. The page does not say who holds the North Ossetian section. Caveat: the lowest-level holder of the South Ossetian section may be Gazprom Yuzhnaya Osetiya, not Gazprom PJSC. Sheet value kept.

verifications.note: Neftegaz December 2018: gas delivered to South Ossetia

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Gas flows through the pipeline according to Neftegaz in December 2018, and a Gazprom Transgaz Stavropol page from November 2020 describes active monitoring of the line. Status stays operating.
